title: Stock Exchange
summary: A deterministic, single-threaded in-memory matching engine per instrument behind a sequencer, with every event journaled so state can be replayed exactly — then trades flow into clearing and settlement.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Place / cancel / modify limit and market orders
Match by price-time priority; publish trades and order-book updates (market data)
Risk checks before orders enter the book; post-trade clearing and settlement feeds
Matching latency in microseconds; p99 predictable (no GC pauses)
Zero loss of acknowledged orders; deterministic recovery

items.label: Peak orders
items.sub: NSE handles billions of messages a day

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: The scale isn't the problem — a single core can match millions of orders a second. Latency, determinism and fairness are the problems, which pushes everything in memory and single-threaded per instrument.

head: Structure
Shape
Why
rows: Bids: price levels descending; asks ascending; each level a FIFO queue of orders
Array indexed by tick or a tree map
orderId → node in the level queue

blocks.caption: Every input is sequenced, journaled, then applied deterministically

items: Gateway validates and stamps the order; risk checks credit/position limits.
Sequencer assigns a global sequence number and writes it to a replicated journal.
Matching engine (and standby) consume the same sequence and apply it deterministically.
Outputs: execution reports to the member, book deltas to market data, trades to clearing.
Single-threaded per symbol: no locks, no contention, fully deterministic.
LMAX-style: ring buffer (Disruptor) between I/O and business logic; pre-allocated objects; no GC in the hot path (or C++/Rust).
Shard symbols across engines; one symbol never spans two threads.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: Determinism is the recovery strategy: same input sequence → same state, so a standby that replays the journal is an exact hot replica.

sections.title: Deep dive: sequencing, fairness, and market data

items: Fairness = one total order of events from the sequencer; ties broken by sequence number, not wall clock.
Market data over UDP multicast with sequence numbers; subscribers detect gaps and request retransmission or snapshot.
Co-location and equal cable lengths for members; speed bumps in some venues.
Circuit breakers / price bands halt trading on extreme moves.

items.title: Trade capture
items.text: Exchange emits trade with both sides, sequence and timestamp.

items.title: Clearing
items.text: CCP novates: becomes buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer; computes margin.

items.title: Netting
items.text: Positions netted per member per instrument to reduce settlements.

items.title: Settlement
items.text: Delivery vs payment at the depository, e.g. T+1 in India and the US.

items.title: Reconciliation
items.text: Member books vs CCP vs custodian; breaks investigated and corrected.

items: Post-trade systems are event-driven pipelines where idempotency keys (trade IDs), exactly-once processing and full audit trails matter more than microseconds.
This is where an interviewer at a bank will probe: duplicate trade messages, late amendments, cancels/corrections and end-of-day reconciliation.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Pre-trade is a latency problem; post-trade is a correctness problem. I'd build post-trade as an event-sourced pipeline keyed by trade ID with idempotent consumers and daily reconciliation against the clearing house.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Hot standby already replaying; failover in ms, resume from last sequence
Replicate journal synchronously to a quorum before ack
Per-member throttles, kill switch, fat-finger price checks

items.q: How do you cancel an order in O(1)?
items.a: Keep orderId → node pointer into the doubly linked FIFO at its price level.

items.q: Why not use Kafka as the sequencer?
items.a: Millisecond latency and partition-only ordering; exchanges use custom replicated sequencers with µs latency. Kafka fits downstream (post-trade, analytics).

items.q: How do you support market-wide auctions (open/close)?
items.a: Collect orders without matching, compute the price maximizing executable volume, uncross once.

items.q: How do brokers avoid duplicate orders on reconnect?
items.a: clOrdId uniqueness per session; gateway rejects duplicates; FIX sequence numbers resend gaps.

items: Price-time priority: best price, then earliest.
One thread per symbol; no locks; no GC in hot path.
Sequencer + journal → deterministic replay → hot standby.
Market data: multicast + sequence numbers + snapshots.
Post-trade: novation, netting, DvP settlement, reconciliation.
